sources.title: Banking sector recovery requires Tk60,000cr annually for 5-8 years: Governor

quotes.text: Bangladesh will need to allocate Tk60,000 crore annually from the national budget over the next five to eight years to address losses in the banking sector, Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman said today (10 October).

sources.title: Tk 60,000 crore annually needed for 5-8 years

quotes.text: Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostaqur Rahman on Saturday said the banking sector would need Tk 60,000 crore annually from the national budget for the next five to eight years to help it recover from massive “financial looting and structural damage”.

sources.title: Non-performing loans again cross Tk 6 trillion

quotes.text: According to Bangladesh Bank data, NPLs in the country’s banking sector stood at Tk 5.88 trillion (Tk 588,704 crore precisely) at the end of the March quarter. By the end of June, the figure had risen to Tk 6.06 trillion (Tk 606,555 crore).

sources.title: Parliamentary body questions 4,000MW solar power target

quotes.text: According to information presented at the meeting, Bangladesh has an installed power generation capacity of 29,000 megawatts, while actual generation stands at around 14,125MW, committee members Nazibur Rahman and Hasnat Abdullah said afterwards.

sources.title: Parliamentary committee seeks more information on rooftop solar

quotes.text: The committee questioned progress towards the 4,000MW rooftop solar target, citing just 60MW added to the grid in the past 30 days, and sought a detailed breakdown of project costs and import data.

sources.title: Govt eyes 4,000MW from rooftop solar in one year

quotes.text: The government is opening up Bangladesh's rooftop solar market to private investment, aiming to install up to 4,000MW of rooftop systems within one year as it seeks to rapidly expand renewable power generation.

sources.title: Eight more die with measles-like symptoms in 24 hours

quotes.text: With these, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,051, while confirmed measles deaths remain unchanged at 104. A total of 955 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 203,848.
Meanwhile, 131 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 22,328.

On 4 April 2026, the National International Health Regulations (IHR) Focal Point for Bangladesh notified WHO of a nationwide increase in measles cases, geographically affecting 58 out of 64 districts across all eight divisions in Bangladesh.
Nine more patients died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours until 8:00am today, bringing Bangladesh's combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,096 this year.

sources.title: Pretty Group factory fire was preventable, probe finds

quotes.text: A district administration investigation has found negligence by factory authorities, lapses by government offices, mismanagement and violations of worker training requirements contributed to the gas cylinder explosion and fire at Pretty Group's factory in Ashulia, Dhaka.

sources.title: No arrests yet over Ashulia explosion

quotes.text: Police have yet to arrest anyone over the September 20 gas cylinder explosion in covered vans and lorries at the parking lot of Pretty Group in Ashulia, Savar that killed eight people and injured at least 25 others.

sources.title: Statement on Ashulia Factory Explosion and Fire

quotes.text: As per the latest information available to the the RSC and Accord, at least 9 fatalities related to the incident have been reported so far.

sources.title: Biometrics to watchlists: Govt eyes automated border screening

quotes.text: The government is moving to engage US-based Securiport to modernise Bangladesh's immigration and border management system, seeking a comprehensive technical and financial proposal through direct procurement.
Bangladesh is working to introduce integrated border management to curb human trafficking and other border crimes and strengthen national security, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said tonight.

sources.title: Dhaka airport's high-tech e-gates that can't even check visas

quotes.text: Installed at a cost of Tk34.5 crore under the “Bangladesh e-passport and automated border control management introduction” project, the e-gates were meant to dramatically reduce immigration processing time - promised at just 18 seconds per passenger.
